title: Restore focus after workflow changes
description: Centralize predictable focus restoration after dialogs, navigation, refusals, imports, update prompts, and PDF generation so focus returns to the initiating or next logical available control.
acceptanceCriteria: Closing or cancelling a dialog returns focus to its surviving initiator
Removed initiators fall back to a documented next logical heading or control
Navigation, refusal, import, update, and generation outcomes never leave focus in hidden or removed content
Focus movement occurs once, is visible, and does not steal focus during ordinary editing

steps.details: Specify initiator capture, successful-action targets, refusal targets, removed-element fallback, and route-heading behavior.
Implement a small presentation utility that restores focus after committed UI changes without coupling to domain rules.
Wire dialogs, navigation, refusals, imports, update prompts, and PDF generation to explicit focus outcomes.
Assert active-element targets for success, cancellation, refusal, async completion, initiator removal, and repeated status updates.

technicalNotes: Maximum execution scope is ten minutes; add one helper and focused named-transition tests.
Status announcement and focus movement are separate; do not focus every live-region update.
